authority: This policy selects WHO does work. It never decides whether work is correct. A route is an assignment, not a verdict.
vetoOrderNote: Evaluated in this order and each is a hard veto, not a weight. Data sensitivity is first because a cheaper, more capable, available model is still the wrong answer if the data may not leave the machine. Cost is last because a cheap model that cannot do the job is not a saving.

orchestrator.description: Plans, decomposes, implements, and reports. Holds no approval authority over its own work.

implementation-review.description: Independent review of implementation correctness and verification of claimed behaviour.

adversarial-review.description: Bounded adversarial pass. Attempts to prove the change wrong.

bounds.boundsNote:
REVISED 2026-08-29 on evidence. This was maxTurns:1, justified as 'one turn forces it to spend its attention on the diff rather than on a conversation'. That reasoning was wrong for an AGENTIC reviewer: turn one is spent opening files, so the run ended with 'max turns reached', no verdict, and USD 0.00717944 charged. Paying for a non-answer is the worst outcome available — worse than paying for a real review and worse than not calling at all.

maxTurns, the wall-clock timeout, no web access, and no sub-agents are bounded execution guards; they do not enforce a spend ceiling. AEGIS separately refuses launch unless a fresh, execution-bound ACP proof shows unified billing, every spend vector at zero, and auto-topup absent or disabled. Authentication is not usage evidence. If ACP reports a tier it is preserved; if ACP omits it, AEGIS records UNREPORTED instead of inventing one. Both shapes require the same zero-metered contract. capUsd is retained only as the owner-approved post-run telemetry ceiling applied to terminal credit-equivalent pricing after completion. It is not billed spend, has no pre-run or incremental enforcement, and one completed event can overshoot it before comparison. maxTurns remains a RUNAWAY guard so a stuck agent stops without cutting off a working reviewer mid-sentence.

REVISED AGAIN 2026-09-01 on evidence, 16 -> 48. At maxTurns:16 a 13-path subject (13 changed files plus 3 pinned specs = 16 files to read) spent its entire turn budget reading, auto-compacted mid-run, emitted `max_turns_reached` and ended stopReason:cancelled with NO verdict, having reported total_cost_usd 0.44160934. That is the same 'paid for a non-answer' failure this note was written about the first time, at a higher number. The binding constraint on this reviewer has never been the dollar ceiling: 0.44 USD against hardCeilingUsd 5 is roughly 11x headroom on money and zero on turns. 48 gives ~3x margin over the file count so reading, compaction and verdict emission all fit; extrapolated cost is near 1.30 USD, which keeps the 5 USD telemetry ceiling meaningful and unchanged. Approved by Marc Papineau 2026-09-01 against the measured run above.
bounds.maxTurnsPurpose: runaway guard only — not a cost control; launch requires fresh execution-bound ACP zero-metered proof and capUsd is post-run telemetry only

repository-guardian.description: Advisory repository-integrity check on a pull request.
repository-guardian.advisoryNote: Cannot approve. Can block on CRITICAL/HIGH. Its comments are never a substitute for a required status check, and no record it produces is accepted by the review gate — the adapter refuses to launch it as a gate reviewer at all, so this is enforced rather than promised.

recursiveDelegationNote: Off everywhere by default. A sub-agent that can spawn sub-agents turns one bounded budget into an unbounded tree, and the failure is invisible until the bill or the context window arrives. Enabling it requires an explicit per-role override plus a declared depth.

PUBLIC.description: Already public or intended to be.

INTERNAL.description: Repository code and process state. Default for engineering work.

CONFIDENTIAL.description: Confidential business or client information. Eligibility must also agree with the Tool Capability Canon ceiling.

RESTRICTED.description: Credentials, regulated health or financial data, and other material requiring the strictest handling.

claude.label: Claude (Claude Code)
claude.workerRouteNote: Concrete worker launch identity for this policy model. The canonical run records the selected policy model and execution; hosting must resolve this declaration and may not choose a provider or Claude model independently.
claude.availabilityProbe: in-process — this policy is read by the running orchestrator

codex.label: Codex CLI (ChatGPT.app)
codex.availabilityProbe: review-adapters.cjs --doctor (local executable check) plus a read-only ephemeral zero-tool probe; the probe result is recorded in the Tool Capability Canon under codex-local

grok-builder.label: Grok Build CLI (subscription failover)
grok-builder.workerRouteNote: Contained implementation-only failover route. It inherits the canonical run objective and packet binding, disables web and subagents, exposes exact file tools only, and carries no approval authority.
grok-builder.availabilityProbe: Pinned local executable plus authenticated subscription evidence; runtime activation still requires the bounded worker containment gate.

grok.label: Grok CLI
grok.availabilityProbe: Pinned executable identity plus a no-session ACP preflight bound to the exact invocation. The proof must be no more than five minutes old, use unified billing, show all spend vectors at zero, and show auto-topup absent or disabled. Authentication is not usage. A reported tier must be a nonempty string; an omitted tier is recorded explicitly as UNREPORTED with a null value. Both use the same zero-metered contract.
grok.costNote: The canonical tool cost class is UNKNOWN. The governed route fails closed until a fresh per-execution ACP proof is bound to the exact invocation, uses unified billing, shows all three spend vectors at zero, and shows auto-topup absent or disabled. Authentication is not usage. ACP may report a nonempty tier or explicitly omit it; omission is recorded as UNREPORTED and never inferred. Eligibility depends on the same zero-metered vectors in either case. Any terminal credit-equivalent figure is recorded only as post-run telemetry; it is not billed spend or a pre-run cap.

copilot.label: GitHub Copilot CLI (repository guardian)
copilot.availabilityProbe: review-adapters.cjs --doctor (local executable check) plus a bounded zero-tool probe with tools disabled; the probe result is recorded in the Tool Capability Canon under copilot-cli
copilot.costNote: Copilot Free was activated on this machine before the probe, and no per-route price has ever been observed. Execution stays METERED on purpose: an unpriced plan is not a proven-free plan, and METERED is what forces a named human and a cap before any route runs.

budgets.defaultMeteredNote: Zero. Metered execution is opt-in per route, never ambient.
budgets.hardCeilingNote: No single route may authorize more than this, regardless of who asks. A ceiling that can be raised inline is not a ceiling.
budgets.meteredRequiresNote: A bare --allow-metered boolean is refused. Spending money requires a name attached to the decision and a number attached to the spend.

fallbacks.note: A fallback is a DIFFERENT model with the required capability. It is never the same model retried, and never a general model imitating a specialist.
fallbacks.fallbackExhaustedNote: When no eligible model remains, the router refuses and the gate blocks. It does not fall back to the orchestrator — self-review is the failure this whole system exists to prevent, and it is most tempting precisely when the reviewer is unavailable.

prohibited: Routing implementation-review or adversarial-review to the same model that produced the work.
Substituting a general model for a declared specialist capability.
Retrying a refused metered route by re-issuing it with a higher cap inline.
Escalating data class to make a model eligible.
Treating a model's self-report of its own availability as an availability probe.
availabilityAuthorityNote: Current availability, with dated evidence, lives ONLY in the Tool Capability Canon. The availabilityProbe field below states how a worker is checked, never whether it is usable right now. Restating availability in two files means one of them is eventually wrong, and the wrong one is always the one that says yes.
